disclaimer: Preliminary Application Exploration Only: The candidate bioplastics below are mapped according to general material property tendencies reported in scientific literature. This tool does not declare any single material as universally best. Real-world food-packaging qualification requires laboratory shelf-life validation for the specific food matrix, formulation/coating grade, storage temperature/humidity, and applicable food-contact safety regulations.

categories.name: Fresh Vegetables
categories.summary: Respiring produce requiring balanced gas exchange (O2/CO2), controlled moisture retention without condensation fogging, and bruising protection.

keyRequirements.title: Moisture Management
keyRequirements.detail: Prevents wilting and weight loss while avoiding excessive headspace condensation that accelerates microbial rot.

keyRequirements.title: Controlled Gas Exchange
keyRequirements.detail: Respiring greens require tailored O2/CO2 permeability (often via micro-perforation or breathable films) to avoid anaerobic fermentation.

keyRequirements.title: Mechanical Protection
keyRequirements.detail: Rigid punnets or tear-resistant wraps protect leafy and crisp vegetables during handling and cold-chain transit.

relevantProperties.whyItMatters: Too low a WVTR traps transpiration water as droplets; moderate or tailored WVTR helps maintain turgor without waterlogging.
Retail produce buyers rely on clear visual inspection of leaf freshness and absence of bruising.
Cold-chain produce environments frequently exceed 80–90% RH, which can soften highly hydrophilic films.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Thermoformed rigid punnets, clamshells, and micro-perforated overwrap films.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Offers high transparency and stiffness at 4–8°C cold-chain temperatures; unmodified PLA requires micro-perforation for high-respiration produce.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Semi-permeable window films or breathable produce pouches (grade-dependent).
candidateMaterials.consideration: Uncoated cellulose swells at high RH; semi-permeable coated grades must be matched to produce transpiration rates.
Pure TPS softens under condensation; commercial polyester-blended grades are needed for wet cold-chain resilience.

categories.validationNote: Evaluate respiration rate of the specific vegetable cultivar alongside film micro-perforation density and refrigerated RH stability.

categories.name: Fresh Fruits
categories.summary: Delicate, moisture-rich crops susceptible to mechanical bruising, ethylene/gas accumulation, and fungal spoilage.

keyRequirements.title: Moisture Control
keyRequirements.detail: Minimizes dehydration shrinkage in berries and stone fruits while avoiding surface condensation that triggers mould growth.

keyRequirements.title: Gas Permeability
keyRequirements.detail: Balances oxygen ingress and CO2/ethylene release to slow ripening without inducing off-flavours.

keyRequirements.title: Damage Protection
keyRequirements.detail: Adequate stiffness and impact resistance prevent crushing during stacking and distribution.

relevantProperties.whyItMatters: Supports protective rigid clamshell walls or tensioned lidding films without tearing.
Governs moisture loss versus mould-promoting condensation inside berry punnets.
Influences droplet beading vs. anti-fog sheeting behaviour on the inner lid surface.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Vented transparent clamshells and punnets for berries, grapes, and cherry tomatoes.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Provides optical clarity and cold-chain rigidity; brittleness requires thoughtful corner/rib geometry.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Studied as thin edible dip/spray coatings directly on fresh-cut fruits and berries.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Research highlights antimicrobial suppression of post-harvest fungi, though standalone films have high WVTR.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Ca2+-crosslinked edible coatings for fresh-cut fruit slices.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Retains surface moisture on cut tissue; requires antimicrobial or anti-browning co-agents and external rigid packaging.

categories.validationNote: Must test post-harvest decay, anti-fog performance, and food-contact approval for any edible coating formulation.

categories.name: Meat and Poultry
categories.summary: High-moisture, protein- and lipid-rich perishable foods demanding strict oxygen/moisture barriers, leak-proof containment, and food-contact safety.

keyRequirements.title: Oxygen & Moisture Barrier
keyRequirements.detail: Controls myoglobin oxidation, lipid rancidity, purge moisture loss, and aerobic bacterial growth.

keyRequirements.title: Leak Resistance
keyRequirements.detail: Packaging must remain liquid-tight against meat exudate (drip) without swelling, delaminating, or losing seal integrity.

keyRequirements.title: Food-Contact Safety
keyRequirements.detail: Strict compliance with overall and specific migration limits into aqueous and fatty food simulants under chilled storage.

relevantProperties.whyItMatters: High water and fat contact can extract soluble plasticizers, monomers, or residual processing aids if the polymer is not food-contact certified.
Low WVTR prevents surface drying and weight loss in chilled retail display cases.
Direct wet-tissue contact and ~90% RH chilled conditions rapidly weaken unblended hydrophilic polysaccharides.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Moisture-resistant rigid trays or multilayer barrier layers.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Stronger moisture barrier and wet stability than polysaccharide films; commercial barrier multilayer designs are still typically needed for long chilled shelf life.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Thermoformed meat trays paired with high-barrier lidding or absorbent pads.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Monolayer PLA lacks sufficient O2/WVTR barrier for extended MAP meat shelf life unless coated (e.g., SiOx) or laminated.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Experimental antimicrobial active pads or composite inner layers.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Studied for antimicrobial surface contact, not as a standalone liquid-tight barrier film.

categories.validationNote: Monolayer bioplastics rarely match conventional EVOH/PA/PE MAP meat barriers; multilayer barrier testing and microbiological challenge studies are mandatory.

categories.name: Bakery Products
categories.summary: Bread, pastries, and biscuits requiring balanced moisture control (preventing staling or crust softening), contamination protection, and appealing presentation.

keyRequirements.title: Moisture Control
keyRequirements.detail: Soft breads need moisture retention to delay staling, whereas crisp biscuits require low WVTR to prevent sogginess.

keyRequirements.title: Contamination Protection
keyRequirements.detail: Physical barrier against dust, handling, airborne mould spores, and grease staining.

keyRequirements.title: Suitable Shelf-Life & Visibility
keyRequirements.detail: Clean optical windows or overwraps with reliable closure or dead-fold performance.

relevantProperties.whyItMatters: Determines whether crisp baked goods absorb ambient humidity or soft loaves dry out prematurely.
High clarity windows and wraps showcase crust colour and artisanal texture.
Prevents puncture from crusty loaves and supports high-speed flow-wrap or twist-wrap operations.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Clear bakery carton windows, twist-wraps, and coated bread/biscuit pouches.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Excellent dead-fold and clarity; coated moisture-barrier grades are essential for crisp biscuits or extended shelf life.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Transparent hinged bakery clamshells and window films for cooled pastries.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Items must be cooled below ~45–50°C prior to packaging so amorphous PLA does not warp.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Short-shelf-life paper-laminated or TPS-blended dry bakery bags.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Suitable primarily for short-term ambient takeaway baked goods where high moisture barrier is not required.

categories.validationNote: Match film WVTR specifically to water activity (aw) of the baked item—high-aw soft bread vs. low-aw crisp cookies have opposite barrier targets.

categories.name: Dry Foods
categories.summary: Grains, pulses, dry pasta, tea, coffee, spices, and powdered mixes needing strong moisture barrier against caking and prolonged storage stability.

keyRequirements.title: Moisture Barrier
keyRequirements.detail: Low WVTR is critical to prevent clumping, caking, loss of crispness, and mould growth during humid monsoon or warehouse storage.

keyRequirements.title: Product Protection
keyRequirements.detail: Puncture resistance against sharp grains/pasta and reliable heat-seal strength.

keyRequirements.title: Storage Stability
keyRequirements.detail: Dimensional and mechanical stability over months of ambient shelf storage without premature polymer embrittlement.

relevantProperties.whyItMatters: Primary determinant of moisture ingress rate into hygroscopic powders, cereals, and biscuits.
Warehouse humidity swings must not degrade the packaging film's tensile integrity or barrier performance.
Resists tearing and puncture from heavy or sharp dry particulates (e.g., rice, pulses, pasta).

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Moisture-barrier layers or rigid dry-food jars/closures.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Exhibits lower WVTR and better humidity resistance than hydrophilic biopolymers; long-term PHB storage aging should be checked.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Short-to-medium shelf-life dry pouches (often metallized or SiOx-coated) and dry-goods jars.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Uncoated thin PLA has moderate-to-high WVTR (~172 g/m²/day at 25 µm), so barrier coatings are commonly required for hygroscopic powders.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Moisture-barrier-coated cellulose pouches for tea, coffee, and dry pasta.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Only coated cellulose grades achieve low enough WVTR (10–30 g/m²/day) for moisture-sensitive dry foods.

categories.validationNote: Accelerated shelf-life moisture-gain testing (e.g., 38°C / 90% RH) is essential before replacing conventional metallized PP/PET laminates.

categories.name: Ready-to-Eat Foods
categories.summary: Prepared meals, salads, sandwiches, and hot-served takeaway items requiring reliable sealing, food-contact safety, and thermal resistance where hot-filled or reheated.

keyRequirements.title: Sealing Integrity
keyRequirements.detail: Consistent heat-sealing or snap-fit lid closure to prevent spills and cross-contamination in transit.

keyRequirements.title: Food-Contact Safety
keyRequirements.detail: Low migration into complex aqueous, acidic, and oily meal components across chilled or warm holding temperatures.

keyRequirements.title: Heat Resistance (Where Required)
keyRequirements.detail: Hot-filled soups, curries, or microwaveable meals require thermal stability above 80–100°C without warping or leaching.

relevantProperties.whyItMatters: Elevated temperatures and oily/acidic sauces strongly accelerate migration of monomers or additives.
Wettable surfaces absorb sauces and oils rapidly unless sufficiently hydrophobic or coated.
Supports structural tray rigidity, stacking stability, and tear-resistant lidding.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Thermoformed or injection-molded trays, cutlery, and heat-resistant lids.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Higher melting temperatures (~145–175°C depending on copolymer) offer greater thermal headroom than unmodified amorphous PLA.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Chilled grab-and-go salad bowls, cold sandwich wedges, and cold deli containers.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Standard amorphous PLA softens above ~55°C and is unsuitable for hot-fill meals unless crystallized (CPLA) or blended.

candidateMaterials.roleContext: Cold sandwich wraps or barrier-lined molded plant-fiber meal bowls.
candidateMaterials.consideration: Pure cellulose does not melt, making molded cellulose pulp useful for hot meals when paired with a safe grease/water barrier.

categories.validationNote: Thermal distortion and high-temperature food-simulant migration testing must match exact serving and reheating conditions.
